competition.flat_book_pnl: A flat seat has zero net financing/competition P&L: paper NAV earning SOFR is benchmarked at SOFR, so those flows cancel, and shocked-risk financing is zero.
competition.funding_basis: Official NY Fed SOFR ACT/360 is the zero-return competition benchmark, not free alpha. Every seat has $100m paper NAV that may be described as earning SOFR, but that capital is equally funded/benchmarked at SOFR so those flows cancel. Deployed shocked-risk capital pays the same official SOFR on trusted standard-shock risk capital: the absolute MTM loss from a 1% adverse spot move, a 100bp (1 percentage point) adverse outright rate move, or a 100bp adverse curve/RV spread move under the trusted duration-1 P&L convention. Equal risk capital receives equal financing treatment across asset classes. Notional is descriptive, not the funding base. A completely flat book — including no-trade-skeptic — therefore has zero net financing/competition P&L from SOFR cash or funding economics. Positive financing/carry alpha requires an explicit markable strategy that earns above SOFR or funds below SOFR. Weekends and holidays carry the last applicable published fixing until the next fixing. If official fixing history cannot be established, new funding accrual fails closed and prior canonical balances are preserved.
competition.instruction: Do not optimize for gross notional or fill available capacity. Size risk from plausible adverse paths and historical excursions while staying inside the trusted risk-capital and drawdown limits. Flat cash at SOFR is the zero benchmark, not a source of alpha. The no-trade-skeptic must include a structured funding_view on every new risk or NO_TRADE thesis: the frozen official SOFR fixing, the relevant SR3 forward-curve view, its own assessment of whether realized funding will print higher, lower, or about the same as the curve, and the implication for remaining at the zero SOFR benchmark versus paying SOFR on shocked-risk capital.
competition.objective: Finish with the highest cumulative net paper P&L across the 14 standing seats.

research_supplement.summary: Overnight tone is firm risk with energy and yields still doing the lifting: Brent at 105.28 and WTI at 92.60 sit well above the stale near-lows narrative, while U.S. equities hold elevated marks against a still-compressed older VIX vintage. Funding stays anchored but not loose—SOFR 3.90 with the front strip implying a higher path—so the warning that 5.5 percent yields could stress capex and the consumer remains relevant. FX is a policy story: the dollar-yen at 156.88 after Japan repeated weak-yen concern, and the dollar-Canada at 1.4166 keeps Canada in the mix. Rate gaps stay divergent: overnight CORRA at 2.30 versus March implied 3.125, while cash AONIA at 4.35 still prices a much steeper Australian path near 5.01 for June. Iran deal pessimism ahead of midterms and Hormuz naval pledges keep an oil premium in focus. The United States, Canada, Australia, New Zealand, the euro area, and Japan are all open for new risk.

carry-is-king.thesis: Cash policy is still easy in Canada at 2.30 and only 3.90 on SOFR, while listed implieds price a heavy hike path. That cash-versus-implied gap is the carry-friendly receive, but Brent at 105.28, WTI at 92.60, and Iran-deal pessimism are the same catalyst that already backed CAD implieds from 3.40 to 3.44. With no open risk, the overnight job is to stay flat: do not re-receive duration, and do not chase AUDCAD parity carry while oil is CAD-supportive.
carry-is-king.invalidation: Stay-flat breaks if oil reverses lower and Iran talks thaw enough that implied hike premia compress while cash policy is unchanged, restoring a patient receive. It also breaks the other way if BoC or Fed cash rates lift, or if Mar27 CORRA and SR3 implieds reprice sharply higher from the frozen prints, confirming energy as a policy regime.

causal.original_belief: Mar27 CORRA implieds at 3.40 were rich versus cash CORRA at 2.30. A patient long receive would be paid as the hike path failed to land, with oil and Iran as background risk rather than the holding-period driver.
causal.observed_reality: The long was opened 19 Sep at 3.40 and closed 28 Sep at 3.44 because oil and stalled Iran talks were backing implieds up. Cash CORRA is still 2.30. Energy remains elevated (Brent 105.28, WTI 92.60) and Iran-deal pessimism is still current.
causal.assumptions_right: The cash-versus-implied gap was real. Oil and stalled Iran talks can overwhelm a CAD receive. Not adding into the backup was correct risk hygiene. Cash policy did not need to have eased further for the structural gap to exist.
causal.assumptions_wrong_or_underweighted: Underweighted that an already-known energy and Iran headline is first-order to outright Mar27 implieds over a nine-day hold. Treated a 4bp implied backup as invalidation while cash CORRA was unchanged. Chose an expression whose beta to Brent/Iran was the trade, not a residual.
causal.causal_divergence: The path was driven by energy and geopolitics repricing CAD implied hikes, not by a change in the thesis variable of easy cash policy versus a rich hike path. Cash stayed at 2.30. Divergence is catalyst dominating carry over the hold.
causal.same_information_counterfactual: On 19 Sep oil was already the live risk and Iran was already fragile. Same information implied either do not open an outright CAD receive, express the gap as curve or cross-market RV with less parallel oil beta, or pre-commit that unchanged cash CORRA means holding through sub-5bp geopolitics.
causal.future_implication: Do not re-receive CAD or US STIR overnight while Brent is triple-digit and Iran pessimism is current. When the catalyst fades, express cash-versus-implied richness with lower oil beta and invalidate on a cash-rate or reaction-function shift, not on the first few basis points of a headline that was already in the thesis.

postmortems.what_worked: Identified oil and stalled Iran talks as the risk that can overwhelm CAD carry, and flattened rather than adding.
postmortems.what_failed: Used a 4bp implied backup from a known energy/Iran headline as the reaction trigger to kill a receive whose thesis was cash 2.30 versus a rich hike path.
postmortems.thesis_assessment: The structural claim that CAD implieds were rich to easy cash was not falsified: cash is still 2.30. The failed claim was that the receive could be held patiently through oil/Iran.
postmortems.expression_assessment: Outright long Mar27 CORRA was too first-order to a parallel oil-driven backup.
postmortems.timing_assessment: Entry on 19 Sep was already inside the oil/Iran regime, so the hold never had a clean carry window.
postmortems.sizing_assessment: A four-basis-point adverse implied move producing a mid-five-figure loss implies the outright was large versus a catalyst that was already visible at entry.
postmortems.lesson: A carry receive is invalidated by a change in cash policy or by a large, persistent re-pricing of the path, not by a small backup in implieds that is the mechanical beta of a headline already known at entry.
postmortems.future_rule: Do not flatten a CAD or STIR receive on a sub-5bp implied backup from oil/Iran while cash policy is unchanged and the cash-implied hike gap remains wide; require a cash-rate shift, an explicit reaction-function change, or express the view in a lower oil-beta curve/RV.

value-guy.thesis: CAD is still the cheap currency: USDCAD 1.4166 sits +1.65 1y z while Brent 105.28 is a terms-of-trade tailwind, and AUDCAD 0.9950 at +1.15 1y z is the same CAD-cheap cross. That cheapness is no longer a rates dislocation. Cash SOFR 3.90 versus CORRA 2.30 is 160bp, and H7 4.705 versus Mar27 3.125 is 158bp, so the 2Y US-Canada gap has already aligned with the cash policy gap. Overnight the book stays flat: residual value lives in spot CAD, and new risk is blocked until the closed SOFR-CORRA pack is fully digested.
value-guy.invalidation: The flat stance is wrong if a new cash-versus-forward US-Canada gap re-opens, or if USDCAD mean-reverts toward z-neutrality while Brent remains bid, which would erase the remaining valuation case.

causal.original_belief: CAD cheapness plus high oil would force the 2Y US-Canada differential to compress, so a long in SOFR-CORRA_2Y_2027H1 at 140.25 was a valuation convergence trade.
causal.observed_reality: The quoted spread moved 140.25 to 148.25 in three days, toward cash SOFR 3.90 minus CORRA 2.30 at 160bp, and the long pack was closed at a loss. Frozen forwards now print H7 4.705 versus Mar27 3.125, 158bp, i.e. the tightness has normalized to cash.
causal.assumptions_right: CAD was and remains cheap on the 1y z. Brent 105.28 is a genuine terms-of-trade support. Cash BoC at 2.30 versus SOFR 3.90 is a large policy gap.
causal.assumptions_wrong_or_underweighted: Mapped REER cheapness onto the claim that the 2Y spread was too wide and must compress. At 140.25 the 2Y was too tight versus the 160bp cash gap, so the value sign in rates was the opposite of the pack.
causal.causal_divergence: FX cheapness and STIR-spread richness are not the same object. Oil and the USDCAD z argued for CAD, not for compression from an already-tight 140bp 2Y. The pack lost because 140bp mean-reverted toward 160bp cash.
causal.same_information_counterfactual: With the same cash 160bp versus a 140bp 2Y print, the rates-value trade was to be long the rate spread, or to skip rates and hold the CAD cheapness in spot USDCAD. The long pack was the wrong sign on the only rates dislocation that then existed.
causal.future_implication: Cross-market STIR is rich or cheap versus the cash policy gap first. If 2Y is already aligned with cash, residual CAD value lives in spot. Do not recycle the closed pack while 158bp tracks 160bp.

postmortems.expression_assessment: Long SOFR-CORRA_2Y_2027H1 translated a spot valuation view into a rate-spread short at a print that was already tight to cash.
postmortems.timing_assessment: A three-day hold cannot adjudicate CAD valuation; it can only adjudicate whether 140bp was tight to 160bp cash.
postmortems.thesis_assessment: CAD-cheap versus oil remains intact. The rates-compression overlay was the error.
postmortems.what_failed: Expression sign versus the cash-forward gap; using 2027H1 STIR as a REER vehicle.
postmortems.what_worked: Cutting the pack once 140bp started normalizing toward cash, rather than adding.
postmortems.lesson: A 2Y cross-market spread is not cheap because the currency is cheap. Screen the spread against cash before invoking REER.
postmortems.future_rule: If the 2Y SOFR-CORRA minus cash SOFR-CORRA gap is negligible, do not express CAD valuation in SOFR-CORRA packs; the residual, if any, is spot.

vol-convexity.thesis: Spot is the wrong instrument for the Iran oil tail and the yen-warning jump: timing is uncertain and a flat book would take unbounded directional risk. The marked hike path already sits in rates, so a curve or front-end expression is a policy-path bet, not bounded convexity on that tail. With no vol surface, no options leg is markable, and staying flat dominates both the rates and spot candidates.
vol-convexity.invalidation: A markable listed vol surface, or a one-way markable rates dislocation that prices the Iran or yen-warning tail more cleanly than cash, would invalidate stay-flat.

swinger.thesis: March 2027 CORRA at 3.125 still prices 82 basis points of tightening from cash 2.30, so a receive that profits as implied marks fall is not dead. Oil at 105 with deal pessimism is an inflation and Canadian terms-of-trade shock that makes 1.7 billion the wrong size on that line, and a second market will not be overlaid to offset it. Cut the live receive hard and keep a smaller concentrated long only because the already-priced hike path still looks rich versus cash.
swinger.invalidation: Kill the remaining receive if March 2027 implied trades through 3.22, if cash CORRA is lifted toward 2.75 while Brent stays above 100, or if the contract sells off another 15 basis points as the oil bid in the Canadian dollar persists.

pragmatist.thesis: Receive Mar27 CORRA remains the book: cash at 2.30 versus a 3.125 forward still pays you to fade a fully advertised tightening path, even with Brent at 105. Deal pessimism and oil are the adverse, but they are already why that forward sits 82bp above cash, not a fresh reason to flip the seat. A 25mm pay in the same contract would offset only a sliver of the 450mm receive, and a 25mm pay in SOFR Mar27 at 4.705 is a US hike-trend sidecar that does not hedge Canada’s oil-exporter inflation channel.
pragmatist.invalidation: The receive is wrong if Mar27 CORRA prints through the 3.13 entry and keeps rising while Brent holds near 105 and cash lifts off 2.30, proving the 82bp cushion is not enough.

grinder.thesis: Official cash SOFR at 3.90 percent is the hurdle on any new shocked-risk pay, and neither Mar-27 implied rate leaves enough residual edge after the hike path already on the screen. Canadian Mar-27 at 3.125 versus 2.30 cash already prices 82.5 basis points of tightening; oil near 105 supports a hawk story but does not cover a fresh 25 million pay once a 100-basis-point adverse move is the shock. US Mar-27 at 4.705 versus 3.90 cash already prices 80.5 basis points, so another pay is SOFR-funded risk into an extended path. The book stays flat.
grinder.invalidation: Stay-flat is wrong if Mar-27 implied rates cheapen enough versus cash that a modest further hawk still covers 3.90 percent SOFR on 100-basis-point shocked capital, or if official cash SOFR falls while those forwards stay elevated enough to create positive carry after the same shock.
